title: How to Store Half an Avocado Without It Turning Brown

seo.title: How to Store Half an Avocado Without It Turning Brown
seo.meta_description: Refrigerate cut avocado, minimize air contact, and use a little lemon or lime juice if desired. Direct-contact wrap slows enzymatic browning.
seo.search_intent: Store half a cut avocado safely while slowing surface browning.

excerpt: Cut avocado browns when enzymes in the flesh react with oxygen. Refrigerate it, minimize air contact with wrap pressed directly onto the surface or a small airtight container, and add a little lemon or lime juice if you do not mind the flavor.
content_html:
A cut avocado can begin browning within minutes. It has not suddenly spoiled: oxygen is triggering enzymatic browning at the exposed surface. The practical strategy is to reduce air exposure, lower the temperature, and optionally acidify the cut surface.

Refrigerate it promptly

Once cut, treat avocado as ready-to-eat produce and keep it cold. FDA guidance recommends refrigerating perishable fresh produce at 40°F (4°C) or below.

Wash the outside of the whole avocado under running water before cutting and dry it. A knife passes through the peel and can transfer contamination from the surface to the flesh.

Reduce oxygen contact

Press food-safe plastic wrap or reusable wrap directly against the cut flesh instead of tenting it loosely over the avocado. A small airtight container also helps by limiting the volume of air around the surface.

Leaving the pit in only protects the area physically covered by the pit; it does not release an anti-browning chemical across the rest of the avocado.

Lemon or lime can slow the enzyme

A thin coating of citrus juice lowers surface pH and supplies compounds such as citric and ascorbic acid that reduce browning-enzyme activity. You do not need to soak the flesh—just spread a light layer if the citrus flavor fits your meal.

Do not rely on water storage

Social-media methods that submerge cut avocado in water are not a good food-safety default. Avocado flesh is moist and relatively low-acid, so it is better to keep it refrigerated, clean, and protected from air rather than submerged for prolonged storage.

A little brown surface is not necessarily spoilage

If only a thin brown film has formed and the flesh underneath is firm, green, and normal-smelling, you can scrape away the surface. Slime, mold, rancid or fermented odor, or extensive soft black decay are different signals and are reasons to discard it.

For a half you plan to eat the next day: cold storage, minimal air, and a light citrus coating are a simple effective combination.

faq.question: Does leaving the pit in prevent browning?
faq.answer: Only where it physically blocks oxygen. The exposed flesh around it can still brown.

faq.question: Does lemon juice stop browning completely?
faq.answer: No. It slows the enzymatic reaction, but discoloration will eventually continue.

faq.question: Should cut avocado be refrigerated?
faq.answer: Yes. Keep it promptly refrigerated at 40°F (4°C) or below.
